operative_quote: We declare that section 204 shall, to the extent that it provides that the death penalty is the only sentence in respect of the crime of murder is inconsistent with the letter and spirit of the constitution
case_name: Godfrey Ngotho Mutiso v Republic [2010] KECA 487 (KLR) (Criminal Appeal 17 of 2008)
notes: Earliest event on s.204. Later held per incuriam by CA Mwaura (E20). Affirmed by SC in Muruatetu (E07) para 52.

scope_text: life imprisonment translates to thirty years’ imprisonment
operative_quote: we come to the considered conclusion that life imprisonment in Kenya does not mean the natural life of the convict. Instead, we now hold, life imprisonment translates to thirty years’ imprisonment.
case_name: Evans Nyamari Ayako v Republic [2023] KECA 1563 (KLR) (Criminal Appeal 22 of 2018, Kisumu)
notes: Life sentence under s.8(2) (paras 1, 3). Para 11: "an indeterminate life sentence falls afoul the provisions of articles 27 and 28 of our Constitution"; para 13: life imprisonment "can be saved ... where life imprisonment has been limited to a number of years"; para 26 then reads life imprisonment as 30 years. Reversed by SC E15.

operative_quote: We hold that the decision in Godfrey Mutiso v R to be per incuriam in so far as it purports to grant discretion in sentencing with regard to capital offences. Our reading of the law shows that the offences of murder contrary to section 203 as read with 204 of the Penal Code, treason contrary to section 40 of the Penal Code, administering of oaths to commit a capital offence contrary to section 60 of the Penal Code, robbery with violence contrary to section 296 (2) of the Penal Code and attempted robbery with violence contrary to section 297 (2) of the Penal Code carry the mandatory sentence of death.
case_name: Mwaura & 2 others v Republic [2013] KECA 541 (KLR) (Criminal Appeal 5 of 2008, 5-judge bench)
notes: Upholds the mandatory death sentence in s.204 and holds CA Mutiso (E18) per incuriam. Appellants were convicted under s.296(2), not s.204; the s.204 holding is reached through the challenge to Mutiso (paras 67-79), hence confidence 0.7. SC Muruatetu para 28 records this holding ("the Court of Appeal changed it holding that by the use of the word ‘shall’ section 204 of the Penal Code was couched in mandatory terms"). Not an appeal from Mutiso (CA 17 of 2008; Mwaura is CA 5 of 2008 from HC Cr A 129, 133 & 134 of 2006), so affects_event is empty (precedent rule, see decisions.md); the status resolver must treat E20 as displacing E18. Itself displaced by SC Muruatetu (E07), which affirmed Mutiso (E07 para 52). Para 79 also covers ss.40, 60, 296(2), 297(2): not recorded (outside focus sections).
